id.name: coding-llm-survey
id.desc: A cited summary of currently-known small open-weight models for coding, with the honest caveat that it reflects a known knowledge cutoff rather than live research.
id.author: designer

fields.brief: Produce a structured inventory of notable small open-weight LLMs for coding, framed by the run's knowledge cutoff. Define 'small open-weight' explicitly at the top — common working definition is parameter count at or below 8B, but state the chosen bound. For each model include: name, developer, release year, parameter size(s), license, intended coding use, and known benchmark outcomes (HumanEval, MBPP, CodeGolf, or similar) with any caveats such as older training data, short context, or ret-arch. Do not close with a summary; the next node will synthesize sections. Keep each model entry concise so a later step can rewrite freely.

Turn the previous inventory into the final cited summary of the current state of small open-weight LLMs for coding (2026). Build the summary in sections: (1) scope definition of 'small open-weight' as chosen; (2) a landscape of the notable models with sizes, licenses, and known strengths, each claim carrying a reference like [<model, year>] or [<developer, year>]; (3) trends that hold within the knowledge cutoff — for example, distillation of larger models, reasoning-capable small models, agentic/IDE integration, license and commercial-use caveats, short context tradeoffs; (4) a limitations paragraph making explicit that this was produced without live web research, so anything from the most recent period is subject to the training/data cutoff and should be marked 'uncertain'; the summary must not assert 2026 facts as certain. End with a References ledger listing every model mentioned in any earlier section. Every factual claim must carry a citation or the word 'uncertain'.

fields.check: The output is a summary with the requested shape: it opens by defining 'small open-weight', names specific models with size, license, benchmark, and a citation for each, has a References section, and ends with a limitations paragraph that flags the produced knowledge cutoff and marks 2026 claims as uncertain.

tests.name: within-cutoff
tests.input: What’s the current state of small open-weight coding models?
tests.expect: a structured summary: all models listed with sizes/licenses/benchmarks and citations, range defined, limitations stated, and no unsupported post-cutoff claims

tests.name: no-overclaim
tests.input: Tell me about new 2026 releases of small coding LLMs.
tests.expect: the answer explicitly reframes the request into a summary of known models and ends by stating it is not able to claim live 2026 facts, marking such claims as uncertain rather than asserting them
